Then the Blessed One, showing that it cannot be spoken of in that way, spoke the verse beginning with ‘for one who has gone to rest.’ Therein, ‘for one who has gone to rest’ means for one who has attained final Nibbāna without clinging. ‘There is no measure’ means there is no measure of form and so on. ‘By which they might speak of him’ means by which, such as by lust, they might speak of him. ‘Among all phenomena’ means among all phenomena such as the aggregates. The rest is clear everywhere.

Evaṃ bhagavā imaṃ suttaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desesi. Desanāpariyosāne ca vuttasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One taught this discourse with arahantship as its culmination. And at the conclusion of the teaching, the penetration of the Dhamma occurred just as it has been described.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

From the Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Khuddaka Nikāya.

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya upasīvasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the Upasīva Sutta in the Suttanipāta Commentary is finished.

7. Nandasuttavaṇṇanā

7. The Exposition of the Nanda Sutta

1084-5. Santi [V 2.0286] loketi nandasuttaṃ. Tattha paṭhamagāthāya attho – loke khattiyādayo janā ājīvakanigaṇṭhādike sandhāya “santi munayo”ti vadanti, tayidaṃ kathaṃsūti kiṃ nu kho te samāpattiñāṇādinā ñāṇena uppannattā ñāṇūpapannaṃ no muniṃ vadanti, evaṃvidhaṃ nu vadanti, udāhu ve nānappakārakena lūkhajīvitasaṅkhātena jīvitenūpapannanti athassa bhagavā tadubhayaṃ paṭikkhipitvā muniṃ dassento “na diṭṭhiyā”ti gāthamāha.

1084-5. The Nanda Sutta begins, “There are sages in the world.” Therein, the meaning of the first verse is: In the world, people such as khattiyas, with reference to Ājīvakas, Nigaṇṭhas, and so on, say, “There are sages.” How is this so? Do they call one a sage who is endowed with knowledge, because of knowledge that has arisen through the knowledge of attainments and so on? Do they speak of one in this way? Or is one endowed with a life consisting of various kinds of coarse living? Then the Blessed One, rejecting both of these, and showing what a sage is, spoke the verse beginning, “Not by view.”

1086-7. Idāni “diṭṭhādīhi suddhī”ti vadantānaṃ vāde kaṅkhāpahānatthaṃ “ye kecime”ti pucchati. Tattha anekarūpenāti kotūhalamaṅgalādinā. Tattha yatā carantāti tattha sakāya diṭṭhiyā guttā viharantā. Athassa tathā suddhiabhāvaṃ dīpento bhagavā dutiyaṃ gāthamāha.

1086-7. Now, to dispel doubt in the assertion of those who say, “Purity is through views, etc.,” he asks, “Whatever these may be.” Therein, “in various forms” refers to exciting festivals, auspicious ceremonies, and the like. Therein, “those who live restrained” means those who abide guarded by their own view. Then, revealing the absence of purity in that way, the Blessed One speaks the second verse.

1088-90. Evaṃ “nātariṃsū”ti sutvā idāni yo atari, taṃ sotukāmo “ye kecime”ti pucchati. Athassa bhagavā oghatiṇṇamukhena [P 2.0596] jātijarātiṇṇe dassento tatiyaṃ gāthamāha. Tattha nivutāti ovuṭā pariyonaddhā. Yesīdhāti yesu idha. Ettha ca su-iti nipātamattaṃ. Taṇhaṃ pariññāyāti tīhi pariññāhi taṇhaṃ parijānitvā. Sesaṃ sabbattha pubbe vuttanayattā pākaṭameva.

1088-90. Thus, having heard, 'They did not cross,' now, desiring to hear of one who has crossed, he asks, 'Whoever these may be?' Then the Blessed One, showing those who have crossed over birth and aging by way of one who has crossed the flood, spoke the third verse. Therein, `nivutā` means covered, enveloped. `Yesīdha` means 'in whom here.' And here, `su` is merely a particle. `Taṇhaṃ pariññāya` means having fully known craving through the three kinds of full understanding. The rest is evident everywhere, as it has been explained before.

Evaṃ [M 2.0311] bhagavā arahattanikūṭeneva desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesi, desanāpariyosāne pana nando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandamāno “etābhinandāmī”ti gāthamāha. Idhāpi ca pubbe vuttasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One concluded the teaching with arahantship as its culmination. At the end of the teaching, Nanda, rejoicing in the Blessed One’s speech, spoke the verse, 'I rejoice in this.' Here too, the realization of the Dhamma occurred just as was described before.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

The Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Minor Texts.

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya nandasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Nanda Sutta in the Commentary on the Suttanipāta is concluded.

8. Hemakasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Hemaka Sutta.

1091-4. Ye [V 2.0287] me pubbeti hemakasuttaṃ. Tattha ye me pubbe viyākaṃsūti ye bāvariādayo pubbe mayhaṃ sakaṃ laddhiṃ viyākaṃsu. Huraṃ gotamasāsanāti gotamasāsanā pubbataraṃ. Sabbaṃ taṃ takkavaḍḍhananti sabbaṃ taṃ kāmavitakkādivaḍḍhanaṃ. Taṇhānigghātananti taṇhāvināsanaṃ. Athassa bhagavā taṃ dhammaṃ ācikkhanto “idhā”ti gāthādvayamāha. Tattha etadaññāya ye satāti etaṃ nibbānapadamaccutaṃ “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”tiādinā nayena vipassantā anupubbena jānitvā ye kāyānupassanāsatiādīhi satā. Diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutāti viditadhammattā, diṭṭhadhammattā, rāgādinibbānena ca abhinibbutā. Sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva.

1091-4. The Hemaka Sutta, beginning with “Those who previously explained to me.” Therein, “those who previously explained to me” refers to those like Bāvari and others who earlier explained their own doctrine to me. “Before the teaching of Gotama” means earlier than the teaching of Gotama. “All that increases speculation” means all that increases thoughts of sensuality and the like. “The destruction of craving” means the eradication of craving. Then the Blessed One, explaining that Dhamma to him, spoke two verses beginning with “Here.” Therein, “having known this, those who are mindful” refers to those who, by contemplating according to the method beginning “all conditioned things are impermanent,” gradually come to know this imperishable state of Nibbāna, and who are mindful through mindfulness of the body and so on. “Extinguished in this very life” means because the Dhamma has been known, because the Dhamma has been seen, and because they are extinguished through the quenching of lust and so on. The rest is evident everywhere.

Evaṃ bhagavā imampi suttaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desesi. Desanāpariyosāne ca pubbasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One taught this sutta also with arahantship as its culmination. And at the conclusion of the teaching, the realization of the Dhamma occurred just as before.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

The Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Minor Texts.

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya hemakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Hemaka Sutta in the Commentary on the Suttanipāta is concluded.

9. Todeyyasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Todeyya Sutta.

1095. Yasmiṃ [V 2.0288][M 2.0312] kāmāti todeyyasuttaṃ. Tattha vimokkho tassa kīdisoti tassa kīdiso vimokkho icchitabboti pucchati[P 2.0597]. Idāni tassa aññavimokkhābhāvaṃ dassento bhagavā dutiyaṃ gāthamāha. Tattha vimokkho tassa nāparoti tassa añño vimokkho natthi.

1095. The Todeyya Sutta, beginning with 'In whom desires…' Therein, 'What kind of liberation is his?' means one asks, 'What kind of liberation of his is to be wished for?' Now, showing that for him there is no other liberation, the Blessed One spoke the second verse. Therein, 'There is no other liberation for him' means for him there is no other liberation.

1097-8. Evaṃ “taṇhakkhayo eva vimokkho”ti vuttepi tamatthaṃ asallakkhento “nirāsaso so uda āsasāno”ti puna pucchati. Tattha uda paññakappīti udāhu samāpattiñāṇādinā ñāṇena taṇhākappaṃ vā diṭṭhikappaṃ vā kappayati. Athassa bhagavā taṃ ācikkhanto dutiyaṃ gāthamāha. Tattha kāmabhaveti kāme ca bhave ca. Sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva.

1097-8. Thus, even when it was said, 'The destruction of craving itself is liberation,' not discerning the meaning, he asks again, 'Is he without hope, or is he hoping?' Therein, `uda paññakappī` means: or does he, with knowledge of attainments and so on, formulate a craving-construct or a view-construct? Then the Blessed One, explaining this to him, spoke the second verse. Therein, `kāmabhave` means in sensual pleasures and in existence. The rest is evident everywhere.

Evaṃ bhagavā imampi suttaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desesi. Desanāpariyosāne ca pubbasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One taught this sutta also with arahantship as its culmination. And at the conclusion of the teaching, the realization of the Dhamma occurred just as before.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

The Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Minor Texts.

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya todeyyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Todeyya Sutta in the Commentary on the Suttanipāta is concluded.

10. Kappasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Kappa Sutta.

1099. Majjhe [V 2.0289] sarasminti kappasuttaṃ. Tattha majjhe sarasminti purimapacchimakoṭipaññāṇābhāvato majjhabhūte saṃsāreti vuttaṃ hoti. Tiṭṭhatanti tiṭṭhamānānaṃ. Yathāyidaṃ nāparaṃ siyāti yathā idaṃ dukkhaṃ puna na bhaveyya.

1099. The Kappa Sutta, beginning with 'In the middle of the stream.' Therein, 'in the middle of the stream' means in saṃsāra, which is in the middle because of the absence of knowledge of a former and a latter end. `Tiṭṭhataṃ` means 'of those who are standing.' 'So that this may not be again' means 'so that this suffering may not occur again.'

1101-2. Athassa bhagavā tamatthaṃ byākaronto tisso gāthāyo abhāsi. Tattha akiñcananti kiñcanapaṭipakkhaṃ. Anādānanti ādānapaṭipakkhaṃ, kiñcanādānavūpasamanti vuttaṃ hoti. Anāparanti aparapaṭibhāgadīpavirahitaṃ, seṭṭhanti vuttaṃ hoti. Na te mārassa paddhagūti te [M 2.0313] mārassa paddhacarā paricārakā sissā na honti. Sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva.

1101-2. Then the Blessed One, explaining the meaning to him, spoke three verses. Therein, `akiñcanaṃ` means the opposite of possessions. `Anādānaṃ` means the opposite of grasping; it is said to be the stilling of possessions and grasping. `Anāparaṃ` means lacking any comparable counterpart; it is said to be the best. `Na te mārassa paddhagū` means they are not wayfarers, attendants, or disciples of Māra. The rest is evident everywhere.

Evaṃ bhagavā imampi suttaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desesi desanāpariyosāne ca pubbasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One taught this sutta also with arahantship as its culmination. And at the conclusion of the teaching, the realization of the Dhamma occurred just as before.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

The Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Minor Texts.

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya kappasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Kappa Sutta in the Commentary on the Suttanipāta is concluded.

11. Jatukaṇṇisuttavaṇṇanā

11. Explanation of the Jaṭukaṇṇi Sutta.

1103-4. Sutvānahanti [V 2.0290][P 2.0598] jatukaṇṇisuttaṃ. Tattha sutvānahaṃ vīramakāmakāminti ahaṃ “itipi so bhagavā”tiādinā nayena vīraṃ kāmānaṃ akāmanato akāmakāmiṃ buddhaṃ sutvā. Akāmamāgamanti nikkāmaṃ bhagavantaṃ pucchituṃ āgatomhi. Sahajanettāti sahajātasabbaññutaññāṇacakkhu. Yathātacchanti yathātathaṃ. Brūhi meti puna yācanto bhaṇati. Yācanto hi sahassakkhattumpi bhaṇeyya, ko pana vādo dvikkhattuṃ. Tejī tejasāti tejena samannāgato tejasā abhibhuyya. Yamahaṃ vijaññaṃ jātijarāya idha vippahānanti yamahaṃ jātijarānaṃ pahānabhūtaṃ dhammaṃ idheva jāneyyaṃ.

1103-4. The Jaṭukaṇṇi Sutta, beginning with 'Having heard.' Therein, `sutvānahaṃ vīram akāmakāmiṃ` ('having heard the hero free from desire') means: having heard the Buddha—the hero, free from desire because he does not desire desires—according to the method beginning 'Thus is the Blessed One…' `Akāmam āgamaṃ` ('I have come to the one free from desire') means: 'I have come to ask the Blessed One, who is free from desire.' `Sahajanetta` ('with innate eye') means with the eye of omniscience that arose together with him. `Yathātacchaṃ` ('as it truly is') means 'just as it is in reality.' `Brūhi me` ('tell me')—thus he speaks, asking again. For one who is asking might speak even a thousand times, what to say of twice? `Tejī tejasā` ('O radiant one, with radiance') means 'endowed with radiance, having overcome with radiance.' `Yamahaṃ vijaññaṃ jātijarāya idha vippahānaṃ` ('that I might know here the abandoning of birth and aging') means 'that I might know right here the Dhamma which is the abandoning of birth and aging.'

1105-7. Athassa bhagavā taṃ dhammamācikkhanto tisso gāthāyo abhāsi. Tattha nekkhammaṃ daṭṭhu khematoti nibbānañca nibbānagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ “khema”nti disvā. Uggahitanti taṇhādiṭṭhivasena gahitaṃ. Nirattaṃ vāti nirassitabbaṃ vā, muñcitabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. Mā te vijjitthāti mā te ahosi. Kiñcananti rāgādikiñcanaṃ vāpi te mā vijjittha. Pubbeti atīte saṅkhāre ārabbha uppannakilesā. Brāhmaṇāti bhagavā jatukaṇṇiṃ ālapati. Sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva.

1105-7. Then the Blessed One, instructing him in that Dhamma, spoke these three verses. Herein, ‘seeing renunciation as safety’ (nekkhammaṃ daṭṭhu khemato) means, ‘seeing Nibbāna and the path leading to Nibbāna as “safety.”’ ‘Grasped’ (uggahitaṃ) means, ‘held by craving and views.’ ‘To be relinquished’ (nirattaṃ vā) means, ‘it should be abandoned, or it should be released.’ ‘May you not have’ (mā te vijjittha) means, ‘may it not be for you.’ ‘Anything’ (kiñcanaṃ) means, ‘may you not have any impediment such as lust whatsoever.’ ‘Past’ (pubbe) means, ‘defilements that have arisen in relation to past formations.’ ‘Brahmin’ (brāhmaṇa) means, ‘the Blessed One addresses Jaṭukaṇṇi.’ The rest is clear in every respect.

Evaṃ [M 2.0314] bhagavā imampi suttaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desesi. Desanāpariyosāne ca pubbasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One taught this sutta also with Arahantship as its pinnacle. And at the conclusion of the teaching, there was the same breakthrough to the Dhamma as before.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

From the Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Khuddaka Nikāya.

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya jatukaṇṇisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Jaṭukaṇṇi Sutta in the Suttanipāta Commentary is concluded.

12. Bhadrāvudhasuttavaṇṇanā

12. Explanation of the Bhadrāvudha Sutta

1108-9. Okañjahanti [V 2.0291] bhadrāvudhasuttaṃ. Tattha okañjahanti ālayaṃ jahaṃ. Taṇhacchidanti chataṇhākāyacchidaṃ. Anejanti lokadhammesu nikkampaṃ. Nandiñjahanti anāgatarūpādipatthanājahaṃ. Ekā eva hi taṇhā thutivasena [P 2.0599] idha nānappakārato vuttā. Kappañjahanti duvidhakappajahaṃ. Abhiyāceti ativiya yācāmi. Sutvāna nāgassa apanamissanti itoti nāgassa tava bhagavā vacanaṃ sutvā ito pāsāṇakacetiyato bahū janā pakkamissantīti adhippāyo. Janapadehi saṅgatāti aṅgādīhi janapadehi idha samāgatā. Viyākarohīti dhammaṃ desehi.

1108-9. ‘Okañjahaṃ’ (abandoning attachment) is from the Bhadrāvudha Sutta. Here, ‘okañjahaṃ’ means ‘abandoning attachment’ (ālayaṃ jahaṃ). ‘Cutting off craving’ (taṇhacchidaṃ) means, ‘cutting off the sixfold body of craving’ (chataṇhākāyacchidaṃ). ‘Unshaken’ (anejaṃ) means, ‘unshaken by worldly conditions’ (lokadhammesu nikkampaṃ). ‘Abandoning delight’ (nandiñjahaṃ) means, ‘abandoning longing for future forms, etc.’ (anāgatarūpādipatthanājahaṃ). Indeed, craving alone is spoken of here in various ways by way of praise. ‘Abandoning concepts’ (kappañjahaṃ) means, ‘abandoning the two kinds of concepts’ (duvidhakappajahaṃ). ‘I earnestly entreat’ (abhiyāceti) means, ‘I earnestly entreat’ (ativi yācāmi). ‘Having heard the Nāga, they will depart from here’ (sutvāna nāgassa apanamissanti ito) means, ‘having heard your words, O Nāga, Blessed One, many people will depart from this Pāsāṇaka Cetiya’—this is the intention. ‘Gathered from various regions’ (janapadehi saṅgatā) means, ‘gathered here from regions like Aṅga, etc.’ ‘Explain’ (viyākarohi) means, ‘teach the Dhamma.’

1110. Athassa āsayānulomena dhammaṃ desento bhagavā dve gāthāyo abhāsi. Tattha ādānataṇhanti rūpādīnaṃ ādāyikaṃ gahaṇataṇhaṃ, taṇhupādānanti vuttaṃ hoti. Yaṃ yañhi lokasmimupādiyantīti etesu uddhādibhedesu yaṃ yaṃ gaṇhanti. Teneva māro anveti jantunti teneva upādānapaccayanibbattakammābhisaṅkhāranibbattavasena paṭisandhikkhandhamāro taṃ sattaṃ anugacchati.

1110. Then, teaching the Dhamma in accordance with his inclination, the Blessed One spoke two verses. Here, ‘craving for grasping’ (ādānataṇhā) means, ‘the craving that seizes forms and so on, the craving for grasping; it is called “craving-and-clinging” (taṇhupādāna).’ ‘Whatever beings cling to in the world’ (yaṃ yañhi lokasmiṃ upādiyanti) means, ‘whatever they grasp among these various kinds of things, such as high and low.’ ‘By that very clinging, Māra follows the being’ (teneva māro anveti jantuṃ) means, ‘by that very clinging, Māra, in the form of the rebirth-linking aggregates, pursues that being by way of the arising of karmic formations dependent on clinging.’

1111. Tasmā pajānanti tasmā etamādīnavaṃ aniccādivasena vā saṅkhāre jānanto. Ādānasatte iti pekkhamāno, pajaṃ imaṃ maccudheyye visattanti ādātabbaṭṭhena ādānesu rūpādīsu satte sabbaloke imaṃ pajaṃ maccudheyye laggaṃ pekkhamāno. Ādānasatte vā ādānābhiniviṭṭhe puggale ādānasaṅgahetuñca imaṃ pajaṃ maccudheyye laggaṃ tato vītikkamituṃ asamatthaṃ [M 2.0315] iti pekkhamāno kiñcanaṃ sabbaloke na uppādiyethāti sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva.

1111. ‘Therefore, understanding’ (tasmā pajānaṃ) means, ‘therefore, knowing this danger, or knowing formations by way of impermanence, etc.’ ‘Observing beings attached to grasping’ (ādānasatte iti pekkhamāno), and ‘this generation attached to the realm of death’ (pajaṃ imaṃ maccudheyye visattaṃ), means, ‘observing this generation in the entire world, attached to graspable things such as forms, etc., and stuck in the realm of death.’ Or, observing individuals deeply attached to grasping, and observing this generation, because of the grip of grasping, as stuck in the realm of death and unable to escape from it—the rest, ‘one should not generate anything in the entire world,’ is evident everywhere.

Evaṃ bhagavā imampi suttaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desesi. Desanāpariyosāne ca pubbasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One taught this sutta also with Arahantship as its pinnacle. And at the conclusion of the teaching, there was the same breakthrough to the Dhamma as before.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

From the Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Khuddaka Nikāya.

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya bhadrāvudhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Bhadrāvudha Sutta in the Suttanipāta Commentary is concluded.

13. Udayasuttavaṇṇanā

13. Explanation of the Udaya Sutta

1112-3. Jhāyinti [V 2.0292] udayasuttaṃ. Tattha aññāvimokkhanti paññānubhāvanijjhātaṃ vimokkhaṃ pucchati. Atha bhagavā yasmā udayo catutthajjhānalābhī, tasmāssa paṭiladdhajjhānavasena nānappakārato aññāvimokkhaṃ dassento [P 2.0600] gāthādvayamāha. Tattha pahānaṃ kāmacchandānanti yamidaṃ paṭhamajjhānaṃ nibbattentassa kāmacchandappahānaṃ, tampi aññāvimokkhaṃ pabrūmi. Evaṃ sabbapadāni yojetabbāni.

1112-3. ‘Meditating’ (jhāyiṃ) is from the Udaya Sutta. Herein, he asks about ‘liberation through higher knowledge’ (aññāvimokkhaṃ), that is, the liberation contemplated through the power of wisdom. Then the Blessed One, because Udaya was an attainer of the fourth jhāna, spoke two verses showing him liberation through higher knowledge in various ways based on the jhāna he had attained. Here, ‘the abandoning of sensual desires’ (pahānaṃ kāmacchandānaṃ) refers to the abandoning of sensual desire when one generates the first jhāna—that too I declare as liberation through higher knowledge. In this way, all the terms should be connected.

1114. Upekkhāsatisaṃsuddhanti catutthajjhānaupekkhāsatīhi saṃsuddhaṃ. Dhammatakkapurejavanti iminā tasmiṃ catutthajjhānavimokkhe ṭhatvā jhānaṅgāni vipassitvā adhigataṃ arahattavimokkhaṃ vadati. Arahattavimokkhassa hi maggasampayuttasammāsaṅkappādibhedo dhammatakko purejavo hoti. Tenāha – “dhammatakkapurejava”nti. Avijjāya pabhedananti etameva ca aññāvimokkhaṃ avijjāpabhedanasaṅkhātaṃ nibbānaṃ nissāya jātattā kāraṇopacārena “avijjāya pabhedana”nti pabrūmīti.

1114. ‘Purified by equanimity and mindfulness’ (upekkhāsatisaṃsuddhaṃ) means, ‘purified by the equanimity and mindfulness of the fourth jhāna.’ ‘Preceded by reflection on Dhamma’ (dhammatakkapurejavaṃ) refers to the liberation of Arahantship, attained by discerning the jhāna factors while established in that fourth jhāna liberation. For the liberation of Arahantship, the reflection on Dhamma—which is associated with the path and has such distinctions as right thought, etc.—serves as the precursor. Hence it is said: ‘preceded by reflection on Dhamma.’ ‘The breaking up of ignorance’ (avijjāya pabhedanaṃ) means: I declare this very liberation through higher knowledge, which is designated as the destruction of ignorance, to be ‘the breaking up of ignorance’ by way of a figurative expression based on its cause, because it arises in dependence on Nibbāna.

1115-6. Evaṃ avijjāpabhedanavacanena vuttaṃ nibbānaṃ sutvā “taṃ kissa vippahānena vuccatī”ti pucchanto “kiṃsu saṃyojano”ti gāthamāha. Tattha kiṃsu saṃyojanoti kiṃ saṃyojano. Vicāraṇanti vicaraṇakāraṇaṃ. Kissassa vippahānenāti kiṃ nāmakassa assa dhammassa vippahānena. Athassa [M 2.0316] bhagavā tamatthaṃ byākaronto “nandisaṃyojano”ti gāthamāha. Tattha vitakkassāti kāmavitakkādiko vitakko assa.

1115-6. Having heard Nibbāna described in this way with the phrase ‘the breaking up of ignorance,’ he asks, ‘By the abandoning of what is it so called?’ and speaks the verse, ‘What is the fetter?’ Herein, ‘what is the fetter?’ (kiṃsu saṃyojano) means, ‘what is the fetter?’ ‘Consideration’ (vicāraṇaṃ) means, ‘the cause of consideration.’ ‘By the abandoning of what’ (kissassa vippahānena) means, ‘by the abandoning of what named dhamma?’ Then the Blessed One, explaining that meaning, speaks the verse, ‘The fetter is delight.’ Herein, ‘of thought’ (vitakkassa) means, ‘its thought, which consists of sensual thought and so on.’

1117-8. Idāni tassa nibbānassa maggaṃ pucchanto “kathaṃ satassā”ti gāthamāha. Tattha viññāṇanti abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇaṃ. Athassa maggaṃ kathento bhagavā “ajjhattañcā”ti gāthamāha. Tattha evaṃ satassāti evaṃ satassa sampajānassa. Sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva.

1117-8. Now, asking about the path to that Nibbāna, he speaks the verse, ‘How for one who is mindful?’ Herein, ‘consciousness’ (viññāṇaṃ) refers to formative consciousness. Then, explaining the path, the Blessed One speaks the verse, ‘Internally and…’ Herein, ‘thus for one who is mindful’ (evaṃ satassa) means, ‘thus for one who is mindful and fully aware.’ The rest is evident everywhere.

Evaṃ bhagavā imampi suttaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desesi. Desanāpariyosāne ca pubbasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One taught this sutta also with Arahantship as its pinnacle. And at the conclusion of the teaching, there was the same breakthrough to the Dhamma as before.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

From the Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Khuddaka Nikāya.

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya udayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Udaya Sutta in the Suttanipāta Commentary is concluded.

14. Posālasuttavaṇṇanā

14. Explanation of the Posāla Sutta

1119-20. Yo [V 2.0293] atītanti posālasuttaṃ. Tattha yo atītaṃ ādisatīti yo bhagavā attano ca paresañca “ekampi jāti”ntiādibhedaṃ atītaṃ ādisati. Vibhūtarūpasaññissāti samatikkantarūpasaññissa. Sabbakāyappahāyinoti tadaṅgavikkhambhanavasena sabbarūpakāyappahāyino, pahīnarūpabhavapaṭisandhikassāti [P 2.0601] adhippāyo. Natthi kiñcīti passatoti viññāṇābhāvavipassanena “natthi kiñcī”ti passato, ākiñcaññāyatanalābhinoti vuttaṃ hoti. Ñāṇaṃ sakkānupucchāmīti sakkāti bhagavantaṃ ālapanto āha. Tassa puggalassa ñāṇaṃ pucchāmi, kīdisaṃ pucchitabbanti. Kathaṃ neyyoti kathaṃ so netabbo, kathamassa uttariñāṇaṃ uppādetabbanti.

1119-20. The Posāla Sutta begins with 'Yo atītaṃ'. Therein, 'yo atītaṃ ādisati' (one who speaks of the past) means the Blessed One speaks of the past for himself and for others, such as 'even one birth,' and so on. 'Vibhūtarūpasaññissa' means one who has transcended perception of form. 'Sabbakāyappahāyino' refers to one who has abandoned the entire form-body by way of temporary suppression; the meaning is that he has relinquished rebirth-linking in the form realm. 'He sees “there is nothing”' means seeing 'there is nothing' by insight into the absence of consciousness; it is said that he has attained the base of nothingness. 'Ñāṇaṃ sakkānupucchāmīti'—addressing the Blessed One as 'Sakka,' he says, 'I ask about the knowledge of that person. What is to be asked?' 'Kathaṃ neyya' means how is he to be led, how is further knowledge to be generated in him?

1121. Athassa bhagavā tādise puggale attano appaṭihatañāṇataṃ pakāsetvā taṃ ñāṇaṃ byākātuṃ gāthādvayamāha. Tattha viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo sabbā, abhijānaṃ tathāgatoti abhisaṅkhāravasena catasso paṭisandhivasena sattāti evaṃ sabbā viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo abhijānanto tathāgato. Tiṭṭhantamenaṃ jānātīti kammābhisaṅkhāravasena tiṭṭhantaṃ [M 2.0317] etaṃ puggalaṃ jānāti “āyatiṃ ayaṃ evaṃgatiko bhavissatī”ti. Vimuttanti ākiñcaññāyatanādīsu adhimuttaṃ. Tapparāyaṇanti tammayaṃ.

1121. Then the Blessed One, having revealed his unobstructed knowledge regarding such a person, spoke two verses to explain that knowledge. Herein, 'He knows all stations of consciousness': the Tathāgata, knowing all stations of consciousness—four by way of formative activities and seven by way of rebirth-linking. 'He knows one standing still': he knows that person standing still by way of kammic formative activities, thinking, 'In the future, this one will be of such a destiny.' 'Liberated': intent on the base of nothingness and so forth. 'Bound for that': absorbed in that.

1122. Ākiñcaññasambhavaṃ ñatvāti ākiñcaññāyatanajanakaṃ kammābhisaṅkhāraṃ ñatvā “kinti palibodho aya”nti. Nandī saṃyojanaṃ itīti yā ca tattha arūparāgasaṅkhātā nandī, tañca saṃyojanaṃ iti ñatvā. Tato tattha vipassatīti tato ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattito vuṭṭhahitvā taṃ samāpattiṃ aniccādivasena vipassati. Etaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathaṃ tassāti etaṃ tassa puggalassa evaṃ vipassato anukkameneva uppannaṃ arahattañāṇaṃ aviparītaṃ. Vusīmatoti vusitavantassa. Sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva.

1122. Knowing the origin of nothingness: knowing the karmic formation that produces the base of nothingness, thinking, 'What kind of hindrance is this?' Delight is a fetter: knowing that the delight there, which is reckoned as attachment to the formless, is also a fetter. Then he sees clearly regarding that: then, arising from the attainment of the base of nothingness, he sees that attainment as impermanent, etc. This knowledge is true for him: this knowledge of arahantship, which arises step by step for that person seeing thus, is unerring. One who has lived the holy life: for one who has lived the holy life. The rest is clear in every case.

Evaṃ bhagavā imampi suttaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desesi. Desanāpariyosāne ca pubbasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One taught this discourse also with arahantship as its culmination. And at the conclusion of the teaching, there was a breakthrough to the Dhamma, just as before.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

In the Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Khuddaka Nikāya

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya posālasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Posāla Sutta in the Suttanipāta Commentary is concluded.

15. Mogharājasuttavaṇṇanā

15. Commentary on the Mogharāja Sutta

1123. Dvāhaṃ [V 2.0294] sakkanti mogharājasuttaṃ. Tattha dvāhanti dve vāre ahaṃ. So hi pubbe ajitasuttassa ca tissametteyyasuttassa ca avasāne dvikkhattuṃ bhagavantaṃ pucchi. Bhagavā [P 2.0602] panassa indriyaparipākaṃ āgamayamāno na byākāsi. Tenāha – “dvāhaṃ sakkaṃ apucchissa”nti. Yāvatatiyañca devīsi, byākarotīti me sutanti yāvatatiyañca sahadhammikaṃ puṭṭho visuddhidevabhūto isi bhagavā sammāsambuddho byākarotīti evaṃ me sutaṃ. Godhāvarītīreyeva kira so evamassosi. Tenāha – “byākarotīti me suta”nti.

1123. The Mogharāja Sutta begins with 'Dvāhaṃ sakkaṃ'. Therein, 'dvāhaṃ' means 'twice I'. For indeed, previously, at the conclusion of the Ajita Sutta and the Tissametteyya Sutta, he questioned the Blessed One twice. But the Blessed One, awaiting the maturity of his faculties, did not answer. Therefore he said: 'Twice I asked the Sakyan.' 'And up to the third time, O divine seer, he answers—so I have heard': this means, 'Up to the third time, when rightly questioned, the Blessed One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the seer who has become a purified deva, answers—thus have I heard.' Indeed, it is said he heard this very thing on the banks of the Godhāvarī. Therefore he said: 'He answers—so I have heard.'

1124. Ayaṃ lokoti manussaloko. Paro lokoti taṃ ṭhapetvā avaseso. Sadevakoti brahmalokaṃ ṭhapetvā avaseso [M 2.0318] upapattidevasammutidevayutto, “brahmaloko sadevako”ti etaṃ vā “sadevake loke”tiādinayanidassanamattaṃ, tena sabbopi tathāvuttappakāro loko veditabbo.

1124. 'This world' means the human world. 'The other world' means what remains apart from that. 'With its gods' means the remainder apart from the Brahma world, endowed with gods by birth and gods by convention. Or, the saying 'the Brahma world is with gods' and similar expressions like 'in the world with its gods' are merely an indication; by this, the entire world of the kind thus described is to be understood.

1125. Evaṃ abhikkantadassāvinti evaṃ aggadassāviṃ, sadevakassa lokassa ajjhāsayādhimuttigatiparāyaṇādīni passituṃ samatthanti dasseti.

1125. 'Thus, a seer of the sublime' means a seer of the foremost, showing that he is capable of seeing the inclinations, dispositions, destinations, final resorts, and so on, of the world with its gods.

1126. Suññato lokaṃ avekkhassūti avasiyapavattasallakkhaṇavasena vā tucchasaṅkhārasamanupassanāvasena vāti dvīhi kāraṇehi suññato lokaṃ passa. Attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhaccāti sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ uddharitvā. Sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva.

1126. 'Look upon the world as empty': see the world as empty for two reasons: either by way of contemplating the characteristic of inevitable occurrence, or by way of repeatedly seeing formations as hollow. 'Having removed the view of self': having uprooted the personality belief. The rest is evident in every case.

Evaṃ bhagavā imampi suttaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desesi. Desanāpariyosāne ca vuttasadiso eva dhammābhisamayo ahosīti.

Thus the Blessed One taught this discourse also with arahantship as its culmination. At the conclusion of the teaching, there was a breakthrough to the Dhamma just as described.

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

In the Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Khuddaka Nikāya

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya mogharājasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Mogharāja Sutta in the Suttanipāta Commentary is concluded.

16. Piṅgiyasuttavaṇṇanā

16. Commentary on the Piṅgiya Sutta

1127. Jiṇṇohamasmīti [V 2.0295] piṅgiyasuttaṃ. Tattha jiṇṇohamasmi abalo vītavaṇṇoti so kira brāhmaṇo jarābhibhūto vīsavassasatiko jātiyā, dubbalo ca “idha padaṃ karissāmī”ti aññattheva karoti, vinaṭṭhapurimacchavivaṇṇo ca[P 2.0603]. Tenāha – “jiṇṇohamasmi abalo vītavaṇṇo”ti. Māhaṃ nassaṃ momuho antarāvāti māhaṃ tuyhaṃ dhammaṃ asacchikatvā antarāyeva avidvā hutvā anassiṃ. Jātijarāya idha vippahānanti idheva tava pādamūle pāsāṇake vā cetiya jātijarāya vippahānaṃ nibbānadhammaṃ yamahaṃ vijaññaṃ, taṃ me ācikkha.

1127. The Piṅgiya Sutta begins with 'Jiṇṇohamasmi'. Therein, 'I am old, feeble, and devoid of color'—it is said that this brahmin, overcome by old age, was a hundred and twenty years old by birth, weak, and would intend to take a step here but place it elsewhere, and his former skin color was ruined. Thus he says: 'I am old, feeble, and devoid of color.' 'May I not perish, deluded, along the way'—may I not perish, still ignorant, without having realized your Dhamma along the way. 'The abandonment of birth and aging here'—explain to me that Dhamma of Nibbāna, the abandonment of birth and aging, which I might know right here at your feet, on a stone slab or at a shrine.

1128. Idāni yasmā piṅgiyo kāye sāpekkhatāya “jiṇṇohamasmī”ti gāthamāha tenassa bhagavā kāye sinehappahānatthaṃ “disvāna [M 2.0319] rūpesu vihaññamāne”ti gāthamāha. Tattha rūpesūti rūpahetu rūpapaccayā. Vihaññamāneti kammakāraṇādīhi upahaññamāne. Ruppanti rūpesūti cakkhurogādīhi ca rūpahetuyeva janā ruppanti bādhīyanti.

1128. Now, because Piṅgiya spoke the verse 'I am old' out of concern for his body, the Blessed One spoke the verse 'Seeing beings distressed in forms' for the purpose of abandoning affection for the body. Here, 'in forms' means because of form, conditioned by form. 'Distressed' means being afflicted by causes such as kamma. 'They are tormented in forms' means people are tormented and afflicted by eye diseases and other things, precisely because of form.

1129-30. Evaṃ bhagavatā yāva arahattaṃ tāva kathitaṃ paṭipattiṃ sutvāpi piṅgiyo jarādubbalatāya visesaṃ anadhigantvāva puna “disā catasso”ti imāya gāthāya bhagavantaṃ thomento desanaṃ yācati. Athassa bhagavā punapi yāva arahattaṃ, tāva paṭipadaṃ dassento “taṇhādhipanne”ti gāthamāha. Sesaṃ sabbattha pākaṭameva.

1129-30. Even after hearing the practice leading to arahantship explained by the Blessed One in this way, Piṅgiya, due to the weakness of old age, without attaining any distinction, once more, praising the Blessed One with the verse beginning "The four directions," requests the teaching. Then the Blessed One, again showing the path leading up to arahantship, speaks the verse beginning "Those overcome by craving." The rest is clear throughout.

Imampi suttaṃ bhagavā arahattanikūṭeneva desesi. Desanāpariyosāne ca piṅgiyo anāgāmiphale patiṭṭhāsi. So kira antarantarā cintesi – “evaṃ vicitrapaṭibhānaṃ nāma desanaṃ na labhi mayhaṃ mātulo bāvarī savanāyā”ti. Tena sinehavikkhepena arahattaṃ pāpuṇituṃ nāsakkhi. Antevāsino panassa sahassajaṭilā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu. Sabbeva iddhimayapattacīvaradharā ehibhikkhavo ahesunti.

The Blessed One delivered this discourse with arahantship as its culmination. At the end of the teaching, Piṅgiya was established in the fruit of non-returning. He then thought from time to time: "My maternal uncle Bāvarī did not get to hear such a wonderfully varied and eloquent teaching." Due to this distraction of affection, he was unable to attain arahantship. However, his thousand matted-hair ascetic disciples attained arahantship. All of them, wearing robes and carrying bowls created by psychic power, became 'Come, bhikkhus.'

Paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

In the Paramatthajotikā, the Commentary on the Khuddaka Collection.

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya piṅgiyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the explanation of the Piṅgiya Sutta in the Commentary on the Suttanipāta.

Pārāyanatthutigāthāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Verses Praising the Pārāyana.

Ito [V 2.0296] paraṃ saṅgītikārā desanaṃ thomentā “idamavoca bhagavā”tiādimāhaṃsu. Tattha idamavocāti idaṃ parāyanaṃ avoca. Paricārakasoḷasānanti bāvarissa paricārakena piṅgiyena saha soḷasannaṃ buddhassa vā bhagavato paricārakānaṃ soḷasannanti paricārakasoḷasannaṃ. Te eva [P 2.0604] ca brāhmaṇā. Tattha soḷasaparisā pana purato ca pacchato ca vāmapassato ca dakkhiṇapassato ca cha cha yojanāni nisinnā ujukena dvādasayojanikā ahosi. Ajjhiṭṭhoti yācito atthamaññāyāti pāḷiatthamaññāya. Dhammamaññāyāti pāḷimaññāya. Pārāyananti evaṃ imassa dhammapariyāyassa adhivacanaṃ āropetvā tesaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ [M 2.0320] nāmāni kittayantā “ajito tissametteyyo…pe… buddhaseṭṭhaṃ upāgamu”nti āhaṃsu.

Henceforth, the compilers of the canon, praising the discourse, spoke the words beginning 'Thus spoke the Blessed One,' and so on. Here, 'thus spoke' means he spoke this Pārāyana. The phrase 'the sixteen attendants' refers to the sixteen attendants, including Piṅgiya, Bāvarī’s attendant, or the sixteen attendants of the Buddha, the Blessed One. And these were brahmins. There, the assembly of sixteen was seated extending for six yojanas in front, six behind, six to the left, and six to the right; in a straight line, it was twelve yojanas. 'Ajjhiṭṭho' means 'requested,' understanding the meaning—that is, understanding the meaning of the Pāli text. 'Dhammamaññāya' means understanding the Dhamma—that is, understanding the Pāli text. 'Pārāyana'—thus, assigning this term to this discourse, they proclaimed the names of those brahmins, saying, 'Ajita, Tissa, Metteyya... approached the supreme Buddha.'

1131-7. Tattha sampannacaraṇanti nibbānapadaṭṭhānabhūtena pātimokkhasīlādinā sampannaṃ. Isinti mahesiṃ. Sesaṃ pākaṭameva. Tato paraṃ brahmacariyamacariṃsūti maggabrahmacariyaṃ acariṃsu. Tasmā pārāyananti tassa pārabhūtassa nibbānassa ayananti vuttaṃ hoti.

1131-7. Here, 'sampannacaraṇa' means endowed with the Pātimokkha morality and so forth, which serve as the basis for the attainment of Nibbāna. 'Isi' means the great sage. The rest is clear. Then, 'they practiced the brahmacariya'—they practiced the brahmacariya of the path. Therefore, 'Pārāyana' is said to mean 'the going to that Nibbāna which is the far shore'.

Pārāyanānugītigāthāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Verses Recited in Accordance with the Pārāyana.

1138. Pārāyanamanugāyissanti assa ayaṃ sambandho – bhagavatā hi pārāyane desite soḷasasahassā jaṭilā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu, avasesānañca cuddasakoṭisaṅkhānaṃ devamanussānaṃ dhammābhisamayo ahosi. Vuttañhetaṃ porāṇehi –

1138. The connection here is with 'They will recite the Pārāyana.' For when the Blessed One taught the Pārāyana, sixteen thousand ascetics with matted hair attained arahantship, and for the remaining fourteen koṭis of devas and humans, there was the realization of the Dhamma. This has been said by the ancients:

“Tato pāsāṇake ramme, pārāyanasamāgame;

Amataṃ pāpayī buddho, cuddasa pāṇakoṭiyo”ti.

"Then on that lovely rocky ground, at the Pārāyana gathering, the Buddha bestowed the Deathless upon fourteen koṭis of living beings."

Niṭṭhitāya pana dhammadesanāya tato tato āgatā manussā bhagavato ānubhāvena attano attano gāmanigamādīsveva pāturahesuṃ. Bhagavāpi sāvatthimeva agamāsi paricārakasoḷasādīhi anekehi bhikkhusahassehi parivuto. Tattha piṅgiyo bhagavantaṃ vanditvā āha – “gacchāmahaṃ, bhante, bāvarissa buddhuppādaṃ ārocetuṃ, paṭissutañhi tassa mayā”ti. Atha bhagavatā anuññāto ñāṇagamaneneva godhāvarītīraṃ gantvā pādagamanena assamābhimukho agamāsi. Tamenaṃ [V 2.0297] bāvarī brāhmaṇo maggaṃ olokento nisinno dūratova khārijaṭādivirahitaṃ bhikkhuvesena āgacchantaṃ disvā “buddho loke [P 2.0605] uppanno”ti niṭṭhaṃ agamāsi. Sampattañcāpi naṃ pucchi – “kiṃ, piṅgiya, buddho loke uppanno”ti. “Āma, brāhmaṇa, uppanno, pāsāṇake cetiye nisinno amhākaṃ dhammaṃ desesi, tamahaṃ tuyhaṃ desessāmī”ti. Tato bāvarī mahatā sakkārena sapariso taṃ pūjetvā āsanaṃ paññāpesi. Tattha nisīditvā piṅgiyo “pārāyanamanugāyissa”ntiādimāha.

At the conclusion of the Dhamma teaching, people who had come from various places, by the power of the Blessed One, appeared back in their own villages and towns. The Blessed One, too, returned to Sāvatthī, surrounded by many thousands of monks, including the sixteen attendants and others. There, Piṅgiya paid homage to the Blessed One and said, “Venerable sir, I will go to inform Bāvarī of the Buddha’s appearance, for I promised him I would.” Then, having received permission from the Blessed One, he traveled by his psychic power to the banks of the Godhāvarī River and proceeded on foot toward the hermitage. Bāvarī the brahmin, sitting and watching the path, saw him approaching from afar, without his carrying-pole, matted hair, and so on, in the guise of a monk, and he concluded, “A Buddha has arisen in the world.” When Piṅgiya arrived, Bāvarī asked him, “Piṅgiya, has a Buddha arisen in the world?” “Yes, brahmin, he has arisen. He sat at the Pāsāṇaka Shrine and taught us the Dhamma. I will now teach it to you.” Then Bāvarī, with great reverence and accompanied by his followers, honored him and prepared a seat. Sitting there, Piṅgiya said, "I will recite the Pārāyana," and so on.

Tattha anugāyissanti bhagavatā gītaṃ anugāyissaṃ. Yathāddakkhīti yathā sāmaṃ saccābhisambodhena asādhāraṇañāṇena ca addakkhi. Nikkāmoti pahīnakāmo[M 2.0321]. “Nikkamo”tipi pāṭho, vīriyavāti attho nikkhanto vā akusalapakkhā. Nibbanoti kilesavanavirahito, taṇhāvirahito eva vā. Kissa hetu musā bhaṇeti yehi kilesehi musā bhaṇeyya, ete tassa pahīnāti dasseti. Etena brāhmaṇassa savane ussāhaṃ janeti.

Here, “I will recite” means I will recite what was sung by the Blessed One. 'As he saw' means as he himself directly perceived with perfect self-awakening and unique knowledge. 'Nikkāmo' means one who has abandoned craving. Another reading is 'nikkamo,' meaning endowed with energy, or one who has departed from the unwholesome side. 'Nibbanoti' means free from the forest of defilements, or simply free from craving. 'For what reason would he speak falsely?'—by this, he shows that the defilements that would cause one to speak falsely have been abandoned in him. With this, he inspires enthusiasm in the brahmin for listening.

1139-41. Vaṇṇūpasañhitanti guṇūpasañhitaṃ. Saccavhayoti “buddho”ti sacceneva avhānena nāmena yutto. Brahmeti taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ālapati. Kubbanakanti parittavanaṃ. Bahupphalaṃ kānanamāvaseyyāti anekaphalādivikatibharitaṃ kānanaṃ āgamma vaseyya. Appadasseti bāvaripabhutike parittapaññe. Mahodadhinti anotattādiṃ mahantaṃ udakarāsiṃ.

1139-41. 'Vaṇṇūpasañhitaṃ' means connected with virtues. 'Saccavhayo' means endowed with the true appellation, the name 'Buddha.' 'Brahme' is an address to that brahmin. 'Kubbanakaṃ' means a small grove. 'Dwell in a forest rich with fruits' means one should reside, having come to a forest abundant with various fruits and the like. 'Appadasseti' refers to those of little wisdom, such as Bāvarī and others. 'Great ocean' refers to the great mass of water, such as Lake Anotatta and others.

1142-4. Yeme pubbeti ye ime pubbe. Tamanudāsinoti tamonudo āsino. Bhūripaññāṇoti ñāṇadhajo. Bhūrimedhasoti vipulapañño. Sandiṭṭhikamakālikanti sāmaṃ passitabbaphalaṃ, na ca kālantare pattabbaphalaṃ. Anītikanti kilesaītivirahitaṃ.

1142-4. 'Yeme pubbe' means 'those who in the past.' 'Tamanudāsino' means 'a dispeller of darkness, sitting'. 'Bhūripaññāṇo' means 'with vast wisdom,' that is, one whose banner is knowledge. 'Bhūrimedhaso' means 'with great intelligence,' that is, one of abundant wisdom. 'Sandiṭṭhika-akālikaṃ' means the fruit is to be seen for oneself, and is not a fruit to be attained at a later time. 'Anītikaṃ' means free from the affliction of defilements.

1145-50. Atha naṃ bāvarī āha “kiṃ nu tamhā”ti dve gāthā. Tato piṅgiyo bhagavato santikā avippavāsameva dīpento “nāhaṃ tamhā”tiādimāha. Passāmi naṃ manasā cakkhunāvāti taṃ buddhaṃ ahaṃ cakkhunā viya manasā passāmi[P 2.0606]. Namassamāno vivasemi rattinti namassamānova rattiṃ atināmemi. Tena teneva natoti yena disābhāgena buddho, tena tenevāhampi nato tanninno tappoṇoti dasseti.

1145-50. Then Bāvarī said to him, “Why is that?” in two verses. Then Piṅgiya, indicating that he was not separated from the Blessed One, spoke the words beginning, 'I am not separated from him,' and so on. 'I see him with the mind as with the eye'—I see that Buddha with my mind as if with my eye. 'Paying homage, I pass the night'—paying homage, I spend the night. 'Therefore, I am inclined in that very direction'—he shows that to whatever direction the Buddha is, to that very direction I am also inclined, devoted, and dedicated to him.

1151. Dubbalathāmakassāti appathāmakassa, atha vā dubbalassa dutthāmakassa ca balavīriyahīnassāti vuttaṃ hoti. Teneva kāyo na paletīti teneva dubbalathāmakattena kāyo na [V 2.0298] gacchati, yena vā buddho, tena na gacchati. “Na paretī”tipi pāṭho, so evattho. Tatthāti buddhassa santike. Saṅkappayantāyāti saṅkappagamanena. Tena yuttoti yena buddho, tena yutto payutto anuyuttoti dasseti.

1151. 'For one weak in strength'—meaning one lacking strength, or one who is weak and of poor strength, and devoid of vigor, so it is said. 'Therefore, the body does not go'—because of that very weakness in strength, the body does not move, it does not go where the Buddha is. The reading 'na pareti' also has the same meaning. 'There'—in the vicinity of the Buddha. 'By directing intention'—by going through intention. 'Connected to that'—he shows that he is joined, connected, and devoted to where the Buddha is.

1152. Paṅke [M 2.0322] sayānoti kāmakaddame sayamāno. Dīpā dīpaṃ upaplavinti satthārādito satthārādiṃ abhigacchiṃ. Athaddasāsiṃ sambuddhanti sohaṃ evaṃ duddiṭṭhiṃ gahetvā anvāhiṇḍanto atha pāsāṇake cetiye buddhamaddakkhiṃ.

1152. 'Lying in the mire' means lying in the mire of sensual pleasures. 'From island to island I drifted' means I went from teacher to teacher. 'Then I saw the Sambuddha'—so I, having adopted such wrong views and wandering about, then saw the Buddha at the Pāsāṇaka shrine.

1153. Imissā gāthāya avasāne piṅgiyassa ca bāvarissa ca indriyaparipākaṃ viditvā bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ ṭhitoyeva suvaṇṇobhāsaṃ muñci. Piṅgiyo bāvarissa buddhaguṇe vaṇṇayanto nisinno eva taṃ obhāsaṃ disvā “kiṃ ida”nti vilokento bhagavantaṃ attano purato ṭhitaṃ viya disvā bāvaribrāhmaṇassa “buddho āgato”ti ārocesi, brāhmaṇo uṭṭhāyāsanā añjaliṃ paggahetvā aṭṭhāsi. Bhagavāpi obhāsaṃ pharitvā brāhmaṇassa attānaṃ dassento ubhinnampi sappāyaṃ viditvā piṅgiyameva ālapamāno “yathā ahū vakkalī”ti imaṃ gāthamabhāsi.

1153. At the end of this verse, knowing the maturity of Piṅgiya's and Bāvarī’s faculties, the Blessed One, while staying in Sāvatthī, emitted a golden radiance. Piṅgiya, seated while praising the Buddha’s virtues to Bāvarī, saw that radiance and, looking around and wondering, "What is this?", he saw the Blessed One standing before him as if in person and announced to the brahmin Bāvarī, "The Buddha has come!" The brahmin rose from his seat, raised his hands in reverence, and stood. The Blessed One, spreading the radiance to reveal himself to the brahmin, recognized what was suitable for both and, addressing Piṅgiya, spoke this verse, "As was Vakkali."

Tassattho – yathā vakkalitthero saddhādhimutto ahosi, saddhādhurena ca arahattaṃ pāpuṇi. Yathā ca soḷasannaṃ eko bhadrāvudho nāma yathā ca āḷavi gotamo, evameva tvampi pamuñcassu saddhaṃ. Tato saddhāya adhimuccanto “sabbe [P 2.0607] saṅkhārā aniccā”tiādinā nayena vipassanaṃ ārabhitvā maccudheyyassa pāraṃ nibbānaṃ gamissasīti arahattanikūṭeneva desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesi. Desanāpariyosāne piṅgiyo arahatte bāvarī anāgāmiphale patiṭṭhahi. Bāvaribrāhmaṇassa sissā pana pañcasatā sotāpannā ahesuṃ.

The meaning is this: Just as the elder Vakkali was resolved by faith and attained arahantship through faith as his foremost, and just as one of the sixteen, named Bhadrāvudha, and Āḷavi Gotama did, so too should you release your faith. Then, by becoming resolved through faith, beginning insight with the contemplation, "All conditioned things are impermanent," and so on, you will reach the far shore of death’s domain—Nibbāna. Thus, he concluded the teaching with arahantship as the pinnacle. At the end of the teaching, Piṅgiya attained arahantship, Bāvarī became established in the fruit of non-returning, and Bāvarī’s five hundred disciples became stream-enterers.

1154-5. Idāni piṅgiyo attano pasādaṃ pavedento “esa bhiyyo”tiādimāha. Tattha paṭibhānavāti paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāya upeto. Adhideve abhiññāyāti adhidevakare dhamme ñatvā. Parovaranti hīnapaṇītaṃ, attano ca parassa ca adhidevattakaraṃ sabbaṃ dhammajātaṃ vedīti vuttaṃ hoti. Kaṅkhīnaṃ paṭijānatanti kaṅkhīnaṃyeva sataṃ “nikkaṅkhamhā”ti paṭijānantānaṃ.

1154-5. Now, Piṅgiya, declaring his own confidence, said, “This is even more,” and so on. Here, 'endowed with eloquence' means endowed with the analytical knowledge of eloquence. 'Having known regarding the higher deities' means having known the qualities that make one a higher deity. 'The superior and inferior' refers to the inferior and superior; it is said that he knows all phenomena that make one a higher deity, both for oneself and for others. 'For the doubters who profess' means for those who, while being doubters, profess, 'We are without doubt.'

1156. Asaṃhīranti rāgādīhi asaṃhāriyaṃ. Asaṃkuppanti akuppaṃ avipariṇāmadhammaṃ. Dvīhipi padehi nibbānaṃ bhaṇati. Addhā gamissāmīti ekaṃseneva taṃ anupādisesaṃ nibbānadhātuṃ [V 2.0299] gamissāmi. Na mettha kaṅkhāti natthi me [M 2.0323] ettha nibbāne kaṅkhā. Evaṃ maṃ dhārehi adhimuttacittanti piṅgiyo “evameva tvampi pamuñcassu saddha”nti. Iminā bhagavato ovādena attani saddhaṃ uppādetvā saddhādhureneva ca vimuñcitvā taṃ saddhādhimuttataṃ pakāsento bhagavantaṃ āha – “evaṃ maṃ dhārehi adhimuttacitta”nti. Ayamettha adhippāyo “yathā maṃ tvaṃ avaca, evameva adhimuttaṃ dhārehī”ti.

1156. 'Unshaken' means not to be carried away by lust and other defilements. 'Unshakable' means unshakable, of an unchanging nature. With both these terms, he speaks of Nibbāna. 'Surely I will go' means I will certainly go to that Nibbāna element without residue. 'There is no doubt in me here' means I have no doubt about this Nibbāna. 'Thus regard me as one with a resolved mind'—Piṅgiya, by this advice from the Blessed One, 'In the same way, you too should release your faith,' having aroused faith in himself and being liberated through faith as his foremost, declares that faith-resolve to the Blessed One, saying, 'Thus regard me as one with a resolved mind.' The meaning here is this: 'Just as you have instructed me, so regard me as resolved.'

Iti paramatthajotikāya khuddaka-aṭṭhakathāya

Thus in the Paramatthajotikā, the commentary on the Khuddaka Nikāya,

Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathāya soḷasabrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Suttas of the Sixteen Brahmins in the Commentary on the Sutta Nipāta is completed.

Niṭṭhito ca pañcamo vaggo atthavaṇṇanānayato, nāmena

The fifth chapter is completed, according to the method of explaining the meaning, by name:

Pārāyanavaggoti.

The Chapter on the Way to the Beyond.

Nigamanakathā

Conclusion

Ettāvatā ca yaṃ vuttaṃ –

And thus, regarding what was said:

“Uttamaṃ vandaneyyānaṃ, vanditvā ratanattayaṃ;

Yo khuddakanikāyamhi, khuddācārappahāyinā.

“Having paid homage to the Triple Gem, supreme among the venerable; by me, who have abandoned minor conduct, concerning that which is in the Khuddaka Nikāya,”

“Desito lokanāthena, lokanittharaṇesinā;

Tassa suttanipātassa, karissāmatthavaṇṇana”nti.

“taught by the Lord of the World, who sought the world's deliverance—of that Sutta Nipāta, I shall make a commentary on its meaning.”

Ettha uragavaggādipañcavaggasaṅgahitassa uragasuttādisattatisuttappabhedassa [P 2.0608] suttanipātassa atthavaṇṇanā katā hoti. Tenetaṃ vuccati –

Here, the commentary on the meaning of the Sutta Nipāta, which is comprised of the five chapters beginning with the Uraga Vagga and consists of the division of seventy-one suttas beginning with the Uraga Sutta, has been composed. Therefore, it is said:

“Imaṃ suttanipātassa, karontenatthavaṇṇanaṃ;

Saddhammaṭṭhitikāmena, yaṃ pattaṃ kusalaṃ mayā.

“By me, making this commentary on the meaning of the Suttanipāta, and desiring the stability of the True Dhamma, whatever merit has been gained,”

“Tassānubhāvato [V 2.0300] khippaṃ, dhamme ariyappavedite;

Vuḍḍhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ, pāpuṇātu ayaṃ jano”ti.

“Through its power, may these people quickly attain growth, increase, and fullness in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Noble Ones.”

(Pariyattippamāṇato catucattālīsamattā bhāṇavārā.)

(By measure of the scriptural text, it is approximately forty-four recitation sections.)

Paramavisuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyappaṭimaṇḍitena [M 2.0324] sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇasamudayasamuditena sakasamayasamayantaragahanajjhogāhaṇasamatthena paññāveyyattiyasamannāgatena tipiṭakapariyattippabhede sāṭṭhakathe satthusāsane appaṭihatañāṇappabhāvena mahāveyyākaraṇena karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacanalāvaṇṇayuttena yuttamuttavādinā vādīvarena mahākavinā chaḷabhiññāpaṭisambhidādippabhedaguṇapaṭimaṇḍite uttarimanussadhamme suppatiṭṭhitabuddhīnaṃ theravaṃsappadīpānaṃ therānaṃ mahāvihāravāsīnaṃ vaṃsālaṅkārabhūtena vipulavisuddhabuddhinā buddhaghosoti garūhi gahitanāmadheyyena therena katā ayaṃ paramatthajotikā nāma suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā –

Adorned with supreme purity of faith, intelligence, and energy; endowed with the aggregate of virtues such as morality, good conduct, rectitude, and gentleness; capable of penetrating the profound doctrines of his own and other schools; possessed of discriminative wisdom; with the power of unhindered knowledge in the Teacher's Dispensation, in the various scriptures of the Tipiṭaka together with its commentaries; a great grammarian; whose sweet and noble speech is born of perfection in articulation, beautiful and pleasantly uttered; a speaker of what is fitting and well-spoken; a foremost debater; a great poet; an ornament of the lineage of the Elders dwelling in the Great Monastery—who are a lamp to the lineage of elders, their intelligence well-established in the higher human states adorned with such qualities as the six supernormal knowledges and the analytical knowledges; whose name, Buddhaghosa, was given by his preceptors because of his vast and pure intelligence—by that Elder was made this commentary on the Suttanipāta, called the Paramatthajotikā.

Tāva tiṭṭhatu lokasmiṃ, lokanittharaṇesinaṃ;

Dassentī kulaputtānaṃ, nayaṃ paññāvisuddhiyā.

May it long endure in the world for those who seek release from the world, showing the path of wisdom’s purity to noble ones.

Yāva buddhoti nāmampi, suddhacittassa tādino;

Lokamhi lokajeṭṭhassa, pavattati mahesinoti.

As long as even the name 'Buddha' of the pure-minded Such One, the foremost in the world, the great seer, continues to prevail in the world.

Suttanipāta-atthavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Suttanipāta is completed.
